title: Предупреждение для Вики  (A Warning for Vika)

segments.t: Determined to expose his rival, Viktor Petrovich pulls art director Vika Goncharova aside in the dining room. He shows her the video of German's brawl in Riga, hoping she will see that the new head chef is dangerous. Let's listen to how Vika and German react in Russian.
Виктория Сергеевна, можно тебя на минуту?
Вика, будь осторожнее с этим Германом.
Он психопат и очень агрессивен.
Витя, зачем ты так говоришь?
У меня есть одно страшное видео.
Там он жестоко бьёт человека.
Витя, ну смирись ты уже.
Герман ни в чём не виноват.
Ты сам потерял своё место.
Виктория Сергеевна, у вас какие-то проблемы?
Я знал, что это когда-нибудь вспомнят.
Идёмте, я вам всё расскажу.
Now let's trace the confrontation between Barinov, Vika, and German line by line.
Виктория Сергеевна, можно тебя на минуту?

'Viktoriya Sergeyevna, may I have a minute with you?' Wondering if Viktoriya Sergeyevna may he has a minute with German shows Barinov caught off guard. Russian packs the whole idea of what is allowed or needed into one impersonal word at the front.
Вика, будь осторожнее с этим Германом.
'Vika, be more careful with this German.' Between the point and the shift, Barinov gives German a quick, grounded response.
Он психопат и очень агрессивен.
'He is a psychopath and very aggressive.' Explaining that he is a psychopath and very aggressive lays the cards on the table for German.
Витя, зачем ты так говоришь?

'Vitya, why are you talking like that?' Wondering why Barinov talking like is cuts straight through the tension between Vika and Barinov. Speaking with the close, informal "you" strips away any polite distance between them.
У меня есть одно страшное видео.
'I have one terrible video.' Mentioning that he has one terrible video moves the talk in a new direction.
Там он жестоко бьёт человека.
'In it he brutally beats a person.' Claiming that in it he brutally beats a person sounds confident, even if German has doubts.
Витя, ну смирись ты уже.

'Vitya, just accept it already.' With the truth and kitchen in play, Vika keeps this short reply brisk and direct. Using the informal "you" shows how direct and unfiltered their kitchen relationship is.
Герман ни в чём не виноват.
'German is not to blame for anything.' Vika explains that German is not to blame for anything, keeping her voice calm and direct.
Ты сам потерял своё место.

'You lost your place yourself.' Realizing that Barinov lost Barinov's place themselves changes how Vika handles the situation. Using the informal "you" shows how direct and unfiltered their kitchen relationship is.
Виктория Сергеевна, у вас какие-то проблемы?

'Viktoriya Sergeyevna, are you having some problems?' Asking whether Viktoriya Sergeyevna are Barinov having some problems puts Barinov right on the defensive. In Russian you say "by me" or "with us" rather than "I have", so the situation sits right with the person.
Я знал, что это когда-нибудь вспомнят.
'I knew that they would bring this up someday.' Even though he knew that they would bring this up someday, German keeps a steady face in front of Barinov.
Идёмте, я вам всё расскажу.

'Come along, I will tell you everything.' Mentioning that Barinov should come along he will tell Barinov everything moves the talk in a new direction. Notice how he sticks to the formal "you", keeping a professional line between them. Let's hear the dining room confrontation again from start to finish.
Виктория Сергеевна, можно тебя на минуту?

Я знал, что это когда-нибудь вспомнят.
Идёмте, я вам всё расскажу.

Instead of believing Viktor Petrovich, Vika scolds him for acting like a jealous child and walks off with German. Listen for the imperative phrase meaning be more careful and the noun meaning video. See you next time!
